title: ALKEBULAN — Ten New Faces
mode: Built-in image_gen, separate re-art-direction per concept
deliverable: Ten desktop website image mockups; conceptual art direction, not implemented storefronts.
reference_roles: Existing African Modern concept: homepage re-art-direction target

concepts.name: Uli / Living Line
concepts.axis: Open editorial canvas with an off-centre portrait and linear drawing.
concepts.summary: Fluid charcoal lines, warm paper and an Ijele portrait; expressive, art-led and spacious.
concepts.direction: 01 / ULI — LIVING LINE. Draw on Uli's fluid linear sensibility and the balance of drawn mark and open space, using ORIGINAL non-symbolic gestural curves. A refined warm paper website with broad ivory negative space, charcoal and tiny oxblood details. Composition: slender wordmark/nav row; enormous two-line high-contrast serif title at TOP LEFT 'A line from' / 'home.' across the left 50%. At right an asymmetrically cropped full-height editorial portrait of one fictional adult Black woman wearing the exact Ijele tee, shoulder-length braids, direct quiet gaze. Behind her, a flat plaster mural with three elegant charcoal swoops and uneven thin lines; visibly hand-drawn, never tubular red wire, never a face outline. Black linework enters the paper margin. A small 'Wear your heritage.' caption and oxblood pill Shop the collection lower left, generous separation. Bottom opens into an offset museum-catalog layout with small flat-lay tee, story caption and thin rules. Unusual asymmetric proportions, lucid modern gallery identity. No dark full-bleed photo, no circle or arch hero. Top strip label '01 / ULI — LIVING LINE'.

concepts.name: Aso Oke / Loom House
concepts.axis: Architectural diptych with textile panels and a burgundy title column.
concepts.summary: Burgundy, coral and woven strips frame a fashion portrait like an architectural facade.
concepts.direction: 02 / ASO OKE — LOOM HOUSE. Yoruba Aso Oke strip-weaving translated into a luxurious architectural web composition. Dominant oxblood/burgundy, dusty coral, champagne woven gold. Precise two-part diptych, around 35% solid burgundy left information column and 65% photographic right stage, not a standard cream hero. On left, huge pale pink elegant upright serif title 'Woven into' / italic 'who we are.' and a sand-colored Shop the collection pill at bottom. Right: tall tactile textile panels assembled from narrow burgundy, natural gold and dusty rose woven strips hang like a contemporary spatial facade, distinct individual warp threads and rich controlled folds. In a deep opening between straight textile panels, one stylish fictional adult Black man wears original Durbar tee and sand wide-leg trousers, full figure, modern editorial pose. Garment remains black and unchanged. Flat cream header runs over both parts, thin oxblood wordmark. Bottom second section a horizontal coral textile-detail strip beside a cropped original Ijele tee, 'The fabric of expression.' Crisp fabric realism, tactile shadows, premium quiet energy; no ribbon loops, basket arches or excessive pattern. Top strip label '02 / ASO OKE — LOOM HOUSE'.

concepts.name: Adire / Blue Hour
concepts.axis: Immersive indigo photographic stage with the headline aligned right.
concepts.summary: An indigo atelier with resist-dye texture and a dramatic, right-aligned fashion headline.
concepts.direction: 03 / ADIRE — BLUE HOUR. Vivid indigo and chalk-white fashion homepage with a nearly full-bleed photographic hero. Evoke Yoruba Adire through real-looking resist-dyed cotton panels with irregular pale circles and dye blooms, arranged as three floor-to-ceiling backdrops in a contemporary photography studio. Original surface studies, not a copied textile. An adult Black woman and man, both fictional, occupy LEFT THIRD of frame at different depths, wearing original Ijele and Dun Dun black tees, relaxed modern denim/trousers. Natural cool skylight, indigo fabric grain, dark skin beautifully lit. RIGHT HALF has large right-aligned ivory serif headline 'Deep roots.' / 'New current.' against an uncluttered deep indigo panel. Small subline 'Heritage, in everyday motion.' and ivory rounded Shop the collection action directly beneath. Header wordmark white and minimal navigation white on indigo. A thin scallop-free horizontal white resistance-mark rhythm punctuates baseline. Bottom transitions sharply to a clean chalk product shelf with two original tees and compact indigo labels. Modern and immersive, rich blue world, sparse carefully set text; no floating shirt over blue ink swirls. Top strip label '03 / ADIRE — BLUE HOUR'.

concepts.name: Durbar / Procession
concepts.heritage: Northern Nigerian Durbar and courtyard space
concepts.axis: Panoramic walking campaign above a bold horizontal type band.
concepts.summary: Sunlit courtyard architecture and a moving Durbar campaign, grounded in sand and rust.
concepts.direction: 04 / DURBAR — PROCESSION. Contemporary Northern Nigerian heritage fashion in a large sunlit earthen courtyard. Warm sand, rust plaster, cobalt detail, black tees. Compose as CINEMATIC PANORAMA: header on warm sand, then wide hero photograph occupying middle 60% of page with two fictional adult Black male models walking LEFT TO RIGHT at opposite depths in original Durbar and Ijele tees with contemporary pleated trousers. Architectural plaster walls, deep rectangular entryways and stepped parapet silhouettes suggest northern Nigerian courtyard space, original contemporary set rather than a named monument. Strong horizontal afternoon shadows, dynamic fabric, no staged horses or costume regalia; equestrian imagery comes from the actual Durbar product artwork. Below photo, large edge-to-edge rust typography on pale sand reads 'CULTURE MOVES WITH YOU.' taking one confident line with clean condensed letters. Small shop capsule and 'The Durbar edit' anchored beneath on opposing sides. One cropped close-up of original Durbar artwork hints at next section. This is fashion cinema with architectural depth and clear cultural specificity, not generic desert tourism. Top strip label '04 / DURBAR — PROCESSION'.

concepts.name: Kente / Colour Code
concepts.axis: Modular typographic triptych based on interlocking woven bands.
concepts.summary: Ochre, rose and forest green form a bold woven grid with confident streetwear imagery.
concepts.direction: 05 / KENTE — COLOUR CODE. Ghanaian Kente strip construction becomes a highly contemporary modular editorial grid. Bright ochre, muted rose, dark forest green, ivory, espresso black, confidently rich and carefully balanced. HERO TRIPTYCH: narrow golden left band with vertical 'ALKEBULAN' secondary typography and original abstract strip weave macro; wide middle ivory panel with huge heavy modern sans headline 'ROOTS IN' / 'FULL COLOUR.' and small dark green Shop the collection button; tall right campaign panel with one adult Black woman wearing original Dun Dun tee, cream wide-leg trousers, sculptural short natural hairstyle. Lower torso crosses slightly into middle panel, face unobstructed. Woven bands of alternating small rectangular geometric rhythm connect photo base to gold left band, original Kente-inspired textile, no false symbolic meanings. Crisp dark green header, clean cream nav. Lower start of collection breaks into two uneven widths with original product cutouts. No cards, no all-over busy pattern, no pan-African flag backdrop. The textile construction determines the entire layout, not decoration pasted on a generic template. Top strip label '05 / KENTE — COLOUR CODE'.

concepts.name: Ndebele / Painted Rhythm
concepts.axis: Graphic courtyard stage with a central photo opening and oversized bottom type.
concepts.summary: Painted architectural geometry meets crisp modern streetwear and playful proportions.
concepts.direction: 06 / NDEBELE — PAINTED RHYTHM. Take the geometric architectural language of South African Ndebele house painting into an original modern retail visual identity. White plaster, charcoal outlines, controlled cyan, orange, grass-green and soft pink geometric fields. Bold but meticulously balanced architectural photo composition. Wide central rectangular door-like photographic opening framed by thick ORIGINAL painted linear geometry (stepped rectangles, nested bars, broad white breathing areas), never copy a specific artist's artwork. Two confident fictional adult Black women in original Ijele and Durbar black tees stand asymmetrically in and just outside this open set, side-by-side at different heights, modern wide-leg trousers, elegant daylight. Clean white navigation above with bold black ALKEBULAN. Main headline BELOW picture, huge clean extra-bold sans 'A BOLDER KIND OF HERITAGE.' split across two aligned horizontal fields; modest black Shop the collection pill at bottom right. Bottom collection teaser uses flat product silhouettes on white, large geometric crop extends over left edge. No circle portals, gradients or random cultural symbols. Pattern is part of built space, typography remains highly readable. Top strip label '06 / NDEBELE — PAINTED RHYTHM'.

Matte espresso-black, warm chalk, dry tobacco brown. Design is quiet, earthy and striking, not generic luxury. Top 20% pale parchment header with large modestly condensed serif ALKEBULAN centered and navigation beneath in a single small line. concepts.name: Bronze / Cast in Light
concepts.heritage: Nigerian metalwork reinterpreted as original contemporary sculpture
concepts.axis: Warm gallery installation with an enormous light typographic field.
concepts.summary: Sunlit cast-metal relief and a Durbar portrait create a warm sculptural gallery.
concepts.direction: 08 / BRONZE — CAST IN LIGHT. Contemporary Nigerian material culture, original sculptural bronze rather than historic plaques. A sunlit gallery art-directed in apricot plaster, brushed bronze, pale cream and oxblood, emphatically a WARM DAYLIGHT design rather than black-and-gold night luxury. Main center-left is huge pale cream serif typography 'Formed by' / 'heritage.' with a beautiful overscale serif f reaching toward artwork. RIGHT HALF: an original abstract bronze relief sculpture formed from modern overlapping ridged metal ribbons and shallow oval depressions installed on a rust-colored plaster wall. Real cast surfaces, warmth, angular sunlight, no faces, masks, sacred objects or reproduction Benin plaques. At far right foreground an adult fictional Black woman wears original Durbar tee, tailored ecru trousers, modern understated jewelry, turned slightly toward camera with print visible. Narrow small ALKEBULAN wordmark top left, navigation top right on peach. Oxblood Shop the collection pill beneath headline. Lower section creamy gallery caption strip 'Wearable works.' with original Ijele cutout and material close-up. Spacious luxurious sculpture gallery, fresh warm architectural composition, no portal ring or floating T-shirt. Top strip label '08 / BRONZE — CAST IN LIGHT'.

concepts.name: Akwete / Future Heirloom
concepts.heritage: Igbo Akwete weaving and contemporary textile installation
concepts.axis: Expansive spatial campaign with a woven canopy and low centered headline.
concepts.summary: A monumental woven installation frames three models in a spacious, forward-looking campaign.
concepts.direction: 10 / AKWETE — FUTURE HEIRLOOM. Igbo Akwete weaving as a future-facing architectural textile installation. Pale mineral grey, deep teal, clear brick red, fine natural flax; bright luminous space, highly contemporary and cultured. Very wide expansive fashion hero filling 75% of screen. A monumental ORIGINAL handwoven canopy with broad red and teal geometric bands and fine smaller cream supplementary-weft-like details bends gently across the upper scene, suspended above a pale floor, individual dense threads visible. No copied traditional symbol, no woven ribbon loops or narrow strip Aso Oke panels. Three adult fictional Black campaign models—two women and one man—with distinct natural hairstyles stand small but clearly readable across the middle ground wearing the original Ijele, Durbar and Dun Dun black tees. Modern flowing trousers; complete visible garment graphics. The architecture communicates inherited craft becoming future space. Headline 'THE FUTURE' / 'HAS ROOTS.' in giant low-contrast fashion serif runs across LOWER foreground, with careful separation from models' torsos; dark teal Shop the collection pill sits just beneath. Tiny minimalist warm-white navigation at top, ALKEBULAN black. Bottom hints at a horizontally indexed archive with one original tee and 'Every thread, a new story.' Editorial installation, spatial, optimistic, spacious. No spaceship, neon, generic cyberpunk or invented history. Top strip label '10 / AKWETE — FUTURE HEIRLOOM'.
